A map in R Markdown, Quarto and pkgdown articles

Source: R/knit.R
knit_print.og_map.Rd

A map printed in a chunk of an R Markdown or Quarto document, or of a pkgdown article, is shown live in the rendered page: it pans, zooms and answers clicks, as in a browser. It is written as a bundle (og_bundle()) and put beside the document as one of its dependencies, as htmlwidgets put theirs, and shown in an iframe; the libraries it needs (MapLibre and the others) are one copy for all the maps of a document or a site. Nothing is served: a map's tiles and data are files in the bundle, so a document's maps want small data (a bundle over 25 MB says so). A layer whose tiles only a server can make is left out, as in og_bundle().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'og_map'
knit_print(x, ..., options = NULL)

Arguments

x

An og_map().

...

Not used.

options

The chunk's options, given by knitr.

Value

The page's code for the map, with its dependencies, for knitr.

Details

The chunk options out.width and out.height set the map's size in the page (by default the page's width and 480 pixels). The document must keep its files beside it, as pkgdown and Quarto do and R Markdown does with self_contained: false; a self-contained page says so where the map would be.

See also

og_bundle(), print.og_map()
